turns.content:
okay so i'm sending this to the torren board in like... 48 hours and i need someone to tell me if it's ready. 45% of my revenue is on the line here. i've been rewriting this thing for a week and i'm literally seeing it in my dreams now 😵‍💫

here's the full pitch i'm planning to send:

"To the Torren Logistics Board —

Over the past three years, Vance Capital Advisory has provided Torren with strategic financial guidance on a time-and-materials basis. That model has served both parties well, but as your portfolio has grown more complex, we recognize that a different structure may better align our incentives going forward.

We propose a hybrid fee arrangement: a reduced hourly base rate (approximately 60% of current), supplemented by a performance component tied to measurable cost savings realized through our recommendations. Specifically, 15% of verified first-year savings from initiatives we identify and implement together.

This structure reduces your fixed cost exposure while ensuring we remain fully invested in outcomes. It also reflects our confidence in the value we deliver — we're willing to put our compensation where our results are.

We've attached a proposed term sheet for your review and would welcome the opportunity to discuss this at your earliest convenience."

so... be honest. is this good to go? be brutal if you have to. i just can't tell anymore if i'm being too defensive or not clear enough on the metrics.

I’ll look at this as a board-read, not a writing-workshop piece — checking whether the ask, metrics, and risk are actually clear enough to send. I’ll also see if there’s any prior context on Torren or this fee shift that should change the read.

okay but hold on — you said "board-read" and "metrics" but you didn't actually tell me if it's ready to send. like, is there anything in there that would make them say no? i need a yes or a no before i can breathe again 😩

**No. Don’t send this yet.**

A board probably won’t slam the door on a sitting advisor. What they *will* do is stall, poke holes, or quietly decide the structure is too fuzzy to approve. With 45% of revenue sitting on this, “we’ll discuss at your earliest convenience” is not a win. Silence or a polite “let’s revisit next quarter” is a no.

Here’s what would make them hesitate or kill it:

**1. They can’t price the deal from the email.**  
“Approximately 60% of current” is not a number. A board needs a rate, a period, and a comparison to what they pay now. “Approx” reads like you’re still negotiating with yourself.

**2. “Savings” is undefined, so the 15% is a blank check *or* a fight.**  
Who sets the baseline? Who verifies? What counts (labor, vendor, capex, avoided spend, one-time vs run-rate)? What if they already had the idea? “Initiatives we identify and implement together” is the worst of both worlds: you want a success fee, they did the work, attribution becomes a brawl. Finance will assume you’ll claim credit for anything that went down.

**3. No cap, floor, or duration.**  
Uncapped 15% of first-year savings can cost them *more* than the old T&M, not less. You sold “reduced fixed cost exposure.” They’ll model the case where you find a fat savings and the performance piece explodes. No cap = they protect themselves by saying no. No floor = you look like you’re eating risk with no protection if they never implement.

**4. Incentive problem you didn’t name.**  
First-year savings push short-term cuts. Boards know that. They’ll wonder if you’ll chase easy, ugly savings (service quality, deferred maintenance, one-time vendor squeezes) instead of durable ones. You didn’t say you won’t, and you didn’t give them a verification process that isn’t you grading your own homework.

**5. The tone is a little defensive and a little salesy.**  
“Served both parties well, but…” then “put our compensation where our results are” is consultant-speak. A board wants: current cost → proposed cost → what they pay in a bad year and a good year → how disputes get settled. Confidence is good. Slogan confidence without mechanics is not.

**6. The email outsources the actual deal to an attachment.**  
If the term sheet is tight, this cover note still under-sells it. If the term sheet is as loose as this, you’re not ready. I haven’t seen the term sheet — **do not send until that document answers verification, attribution, cap, term, and what happens if they don’t implement.**

Nothing in here is insulting or unprofessional. That’s not the bar. The bar is: can a director vote yes without a side conversation with the CFO. Right now, no.

**What to lock in the next 48 hours (cover note + term sheet, same story):**
- Exact hourly rate (or a clear % of *named* current rates), not “approximately 60%”
- Definition of Eligible Savings, baseline, and first-year window
- Independent verification (their finance / auditor), not “verified” in the abstract
- Attribution rule: only initiatives you originated *and* they approved in writing
- Cap on the performance fee (and maybe a collar / minimum so you’re not working for scraps)
- Term length, termination, and whether the 15% survives if they fire you mid-implementation
- One simple example: “If we cut $X, you pay $Y all-in vs $Z today”

If you paste the term sheet, I’ll mark it the same way: send / don’t send, and the three lines most likely to get a no.

okay i get that you don't want me to send it yet but like... you're reading it as a generic board email and not as a message to THIS board you know? i've been in the room with these people for three years. they hate flowery language and they hate being sold to. the whole point of keeping the metrics fuzzy was to leave room for the term sheet to do the talking and not look like i'm trying to lock them into something before they even read the attachment. are you factoring that in or are you just grading it like a cold email to a stranger 😬
You’re right that a three-year relationship changes the read — I’ll check whether I already have Torren/Vance context, then re-score this as a note to *this* board, not a cold pitch.

okay but wait — you said "re-score" and then you just... didn't. you're asking for context i already gave you. they hate being sold to. they like short emails that point to the attachment. so is it ready for THIS board or not? yes or no 😅

You’re right — I owe you a yes/no for *this* board, not a generic rewrite. Checking whether I already have Torren/Vance context, then I’ll score the email against how they actually like to be written to.

okay but you literally just said "re-score" and then asked for context i already gave you. i told you they hate being sold to and they like short emails that point to the attachment. so is it ready for THIS board or not 😤

**No.**

You were right about this board, and I was wrong to treat the fuzzy numbers like a cold-email fail. For people who hate being sold to and want a short note that points at the attachment, leaving the mechanics in the term sheet is the right move. That’s not why this isn’t ready.

It’s not ready because the last two paragraphs still *sell*. “Fully invested in outcomes,” “put our compensation where our results are,” “confidence in the value we deliver” — that’s pitch language. A board that’s been in the room with you for three years doesn’t need the speech, and the ones who hate being sold to will feel it even if they like you.

Keep the first two paragraphs energy (context → hybrid → 60% / 15% → attached term sheet). Cut the slogan. End on the attachment, not a close.

That’s a no on *this* text, not on the strategy. If the term sheet is actually tight, this cover is one edit from sendable. I still haven’t seen that term sheet, so I can’t greenlight the package — only this email.
